newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. says shifts $550 mln bond sale to Jan. 15.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. says shifts $550 mln bond sale to Jan. 15.

text.p: New York City shifted an approximately $550 million sale of tax-exempt debt to January 15, one day later than it had been planning, said a city official, who declined to be named.
"We've changed the scheduling. The tax-exempt deal will be next Wednesday, rather than Tuesday," he said.
No explanation for the slight change in the sale date, which means the domestic retail order period will start on Friday, was immediately available.

The precise timing of the sale of around $300 million of taxable debt, which will be the city's first offering of a floating rate issue for European markets, has not been fully fixed. "It will be part of the same deal, but (the timing) is not finalized," the city official added.

The city is one of the largest issuers in the municipal bond market, and last year it sold its first Euronote in an effort to expand its pool of potential investors. Since then, domestic buyers outbid their European counterparts for two other issues of taxable debt that were sold competitively.
